## Reviewers request

The manuscript lacks an appropriate statistical framework for the field data. The most important weakness is the treatment of field detections as independent observations. The design is inherently hierarchical (8 localities, sampled 3 times, 5 sites pooled per locality, 3 filter types, 3 replicate filters, 3 technical amplification replicates), yet most results are summarized as counts, positivity rates, or scores. **A more appropriate analysis would involve a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) framework, possibly using locality as a random effect, sampling event as a repeated factor, filter type as fixed effect, assay type as fixed effect, turbidity as covariate.**

At present it is difficult to determine whether apparent differences among filter types or assays remain significant after accounting for repeated sampling and non-independence. The current use of ANOVA appears restricted primarily to laboratory experiments and filtered volume comparisons.

# Data 

```{r}
str(data)
sum(is.na(data$presence))
with(data, table(amplificance_method, is.na(presence)))

data <- data |>
  mutate(across(c(location, season, filter, amplificance_method, samplingId), factor),
         volume   = as.numeric( trimws(volume, whitespace = "[ \\h\\v]") ), # trim unicode ws too
         presence = as.integer(presence))



snail <- data |>
  filter(amplificance_method == "snail") |>
  group_by(samplingId) |>
  summarise(snail = as.integer(any(presence == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
            consistent = n_distinct(na.omit(presence)) <= 1, .groups = "drop")

all(snail$consistent)

edna <- data |>
  filter(amplificance_method != "snail", !is.na(presence)) |>
  droplevels() |>
  left_join(snail, by = "samplingId") |>
  mutate(sampleId = interaction(samplingId, filter, replication, drop = TRUE),
         turb_z   = as.numeric(scale(log(turbidity))),
         amplificance_method = relevel(amplificance_method, "qPCR"))

edna_agg <- edna |>
  group_by(location, season, samplingId, sampleId, filter, amplificance_method, turb_z, snail) |>
  summarise(pos = sum(presence), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
ev_edna <- edna |>
  mutate(method = interaction(filter, amplificance_method, sep = "_", drop = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(location, season, samplingId, method) |>
  summarise(pos = as.integer(any(presence == 1)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(method = as.character(method))

ev_snail <- snail |>
  left_join(distinct(edna, samplingId, location, season), by = "samplingId") |>
  transmute(location, season, samplingId, method = "snail", pos = snail)

ev <- bind_rows(ev_edna, ev_snail) |>
  mutate(method = relevel(factor(method), ref = "snail"))
```

```{r}
# function for calc payoff matrix from the article
score_fun <- function(pos, snail, M = c(TP = 1, FN = -1, FP = 0, TN = 0)) {
  unname(ifelse(pos == 1 & snail == 1, M["TP"],
         ifelse(pos == 0 & snail == 1, M["FN"],
         ifelse(pos == 1 & snail == 0, M["FP"], M["TN"]))))
}

ev2 <- ev |>
  filter(method != "snail") |> droplevels() |>
  left_join(select(snail, samplingId, snail), by = "samplingId") |>
  mutate(match = as.integer(pos == snail),
         score = score_fun(pos, snail))
```

```{r}
edna_plus_env <- merge(edna |> select(!turbidity & !samplingId), env |> select(!presence), by=c("location", "date"), all.x = T)
```

# stat 1

- `season` should be random effect?
- `sampleId` is made from `samplingID` (`location` + `date`) + `filter` + `replication` $\to$ should I discard some re?
- maybe easiest is to make a full model and then do model selection on it (exclude turbulence, etc)

```{r}
m1 <- glmmTMB(presence ~ filter * amplificance_method + turb_z + season +
                (1 | location) + (1 | samplingId) + (1 | sampleId),
              family = binomial, data = edna)

m2 <- update(m1, . ~ . + filter:turb_z)      # does turbidity affect filters differently?
anova(m1, m2)
```

m1 AIC is smaller, btw anova non-sign $\to$ proceed with m1

```{r}
summary(m1)
Anova(m1, type = "II")
```

filter type and amplification method is signif. Interesting is, that their interaction is also signif.

## diagnostics

```{r}
res <- simulateResiduals(m1)
plot(res)
testDispersion(res)
```

# stat 5

Event-level agreement with snails (sensitivity / specificity per filter × method)

- sensitivity: percent when par detected (in cases when snails confirm par presence)
- specificity: percent when par not detected (when sampled snails did not have parasites)

```{r}
edna |>
  group_by(samplingId, filter, amplificance_method, snail) |>
  summarise(edna_pos = as.integer(any(presence == 1)), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(filter, amplificance_method) |>
  summarise(sensitivity = mean(edna_pos[snail == 1]),
            specificity = 1 - mean(edna_pos[snail == 0]),
            n_snail_pos = sum(snail == 1),
            n_snail_neg = sum(snail == 0),
            .groups = "drop")
```

sensitivity with n=5 it would not be wise to publish. `binom.test` could be used to calculate conf intervals

```{r}
ev |>
  filter(method != "snail") |>
  left_join(select(snail, samplingId, snail), by = "samplingId") |>
  group_by(method) |>
  summarise(TP = sum(pos == 1 & snail == 1), FN = sum(pos == 0 & snail == 1),
            TN = sum(pos == 0 & snail == 0), FP = sum(pos == 1 & snail == 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sens = TP / (TP + FN),
         sens_lo = binom.test(TP, TP + FN)$conf.int[1], sens_hi = binom.test(TP, TP + FN)$conf.int[2],
         spec = TN / (TN + FP),
         spec_lo = binom.test(TN, TN + FP)$conf.int[1], spec_hi = binom.test(TN, TN + FP)$conf.int[2],
         concord = (TP + TN) / 24,
         kappa = { po <- (TP+TN)/24; pe <- ((TP+FN)*(TP+FP) + (TN+FP)*(TN+FN))/24^2; (po-pe)/(1-pe) }) |>
  ungroup()
```

Well, nothing is significant, ignore this one.

# stat 7

same as first, but with a factor of full combination of methods

this way the lack of RAA tests wont be disturbing the interpretation of resutls

```{r}
edna$fm <- interaction(edna$filter, edna$amplificance_method, drop = TRUE, sep = "_")
mC <- update(m1, . ~ fm + turb_z + season + (1|location) + (1|samplingId) + (1|sampleId))
emmeans(mC, pairwise ~ fm, type = "response")
```

## spec contrasts

```{r}
emm <- emmeans(mC, ~ fm)
lv  <- levels(edna$fm)
L   <- function(a, b) { v <- setNames(rep(0, length(lv)), lv); v[a] <- 1; v[b] <- -1; v }
cons <- list(
  "qPCR: A vs B" = L("A_qPCR","B_qPCR"), "qPCR: A vs C" = L("A_qPCR","C_qPCR"), "qPCR: B vs C" = L("B_qPCR","C_qPCR"),
  "LAMP: A vs B" = L("A_LAMP","B_LAMP"), "LAMP: A vs C" = L("A_LAMP","C_LAMP"), "LAMP: B vs C" = L("B_LAMP","C_LAMP"),
  "C: qPCR vs LAMP" = L("C_qPCR","C_LAMP"), "C: qPCR vs RAA" = L("C_qPCR","C_RAA"), "C: LAMP vs RAA" = L("C_LAMP","C_RAA"))
contrast(emm, cons, adjust = "holm", type = "response")   # odds ratios
```

```{r}
emm <- emmeans(mC, ~ fm)
contrast(emm, "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = which(levels(emm)$fm == "C_qPCR"),
         type = "response", reverse = TRUE)   # odds ratios C_qPCR / others, Dunnett-adjusted
```


# stat 8

aggregate filter and method
add snail
and handle snail as reference

```{r}
with(ev, tapply(pos, method, sum))          # events positive, out of 24

m_ev <- glmmTMB(pos ~ method + season + (1 | location) + (1 | samplingId),
                family = binomial, data = ev)
summary(m_ev)
emmeans(m_ev, trt.vs.ctrl ~ method, ref = "snail", type = "response")  
```

odds ratio is 1 for filter A and qPCR

```{r}
ord <- c("snail","A_qPCR","B_qPCR","C_qPCR","A_LAMP","B_LAMP","C_LAMP","C_RAA")

ct <- confint(contrast(emmeans(m_ev, ~ method), "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, type = "response"))
ct$method <- sub(" / snail", "", ct$contrast)
ggplot(ct, aes(odds.ratio, factor(method, rev(ord[-1])))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = asymp.LCL, xmax = asymp.UCL)) +
  scale_x_log10() + labs(x = "Odds ratio vs snail survey (log scale)", y = NULL) + theme_bw()
```


```{r}
ev_plot <- ev |>
  left_join(select(snail, samplingId, snail), by = "samplingId") |>
  mutate(status = case_when(method == "snail" & pos == 1 ~ "Snail +",
                            method == "snail"            ~ "Snail −",
                            pos == 1 & snail == 1 ~ "Both +",
                            pos == 1 & snail == 0 ~ "eDNA + only",
                            pos == 0 & snail == 1 ~ "Snail + only",
                            TRUE                  ~ "Both −"),
         method = factor(method, ord))

ggplot(ev_plot, aes(method, samplingId, fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  facet_grid(location ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Both +" = "#1b7837", "eDNA + only" = "#e08214",
                               "Snail + only" = "#b2182b", "Both −" = "grey90",
                               "Snail +" = "black", "Snail −" = "grey70")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sampling event", fill = NULL) + theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

filterC qPCR and RAA is different from snail

# stat 10

payoff matrix

|                | found in snail | not found in snail |
|----------------|----------------|--------------------|
| found eDNA     |        1       |           0        |
| not found eDNA |      -1        |           0        |       

```{r}
ev2 |>
  group_by(method) |>
  summarise(n_match = sum(match), concord = mean(match),
            conc_lo = binom.test(sum(match), n())$conf.int[1],
            conc_hi = binom.test(sum(match), n())$conf.int[2],
            score_total = sum(score),
            score_mean  = mean(score[snail == 1]), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(score_total))

# friedman.test(score ~ method | samplingId, data = subset(ev2, snail == 1))
```

## changing the payoff

```{r}
w <- seq(0, -1, by = -0.05)
sweep <- purrr::map_dfr(w, 
                        \(wfp) ev2 |>
                          mutate(s = score_fun(pos, snail, c(TP = 1, FN = -1, FP = wfp, TN = 0))) |>
                          group_by(method) |> 
                          summarise(score = sum(s), .groups = "drop") 
                        |> mutate(FP_weight = wfp)
                        )

ggplot(sweep, aes(FP_weight, score, colour = method)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_reverse() + 
  labs(x = "Payoff for eDNA+ / snail− (FP weight)", y = "Total score") + 
  theme_bw()
```

Well, as when snail==0 if is 0, it is the same as stat4

# stat11

Same as stat7, but with all environment variables from `edna_plus_env`

# Conclusions

- dont use stat1 and stat2, instead use stat7 or stat6
- compared with snails, A_qPCR is closest
- c_QPCR is the most sensitive (stat7: 0.2365) and differs from others significantly (stat7 contrasts)
- stat3: indeed, molecular methods show something similar to snail data
- 3 methods to compare it with snail data. Which one is the best?
  - stat4: drop data where snail+presence == 0 -> 0: did not find it, where it should, 1: it found it
  - stat8: aggregate molecular data and add snail as an equal level method, then contrast it with snail as reference
  - stat9: concordance test: snail presence == eDNA presence
